why: E21 (PRED-020) and its replication E22 (PRED-021: R1 PASS, share of a in T 0.52 on seeds 2201-2206; pooled 12-seed margin lower bound 0.0006, barely > 0) found that fcfs's extra delay under fragmentation is about half or more state coupling a = log(J_F / J_CS): shuffling F's slowdowns within need class (CS) removes it. CS breaks two links at once: the link between a slowdown and the cluster state it was placed into, and its link with neighbours in arrival order. C-058 records the placement-time state and asks which link carries a, by shuffling within finer strata that keep one link and not the other.

inherits.changed: seeds 2301-2306 (never used); run_e20.one gains an opt-in C-058 mode (sixth task element {'c058': True}); sim.simulate gains an optional read-only trace= argument; runner run_e23.py; grader analyze_e23.py.

instrument.trace: Every placement appends (jid, t, need, excess_nodes, rate, busy, n_waiting, n_free, free_nodes_any, free_nodes_full). busy = servers held by other jobs at that moment; n_waiting = jobs waiting at the decision epoch before admission; scatter = free_nodes_any - ceil(n_free / 8). Recorded in BASE (pi 0: placement and excess are the same rule, with no slowdown) and F, for fcfs and srpt; summarised per need class over measured jobs (jid >= 20% of n) as Spearman correlations of excess with busy, n_waiting and scatter, and mean excess by busy and queue bins.
instrument.new_arms: fcfs only, pi = 0, same arrivals/needs/sizes, F's per-job slowdowns permuted within need class AND a stratum: CO = five bins of F's busy servers at that job's placement (value quantiles, ties kept together), CQ = five bins of F's queue length at placement, CT = five equal-count arrival-order blocks. Each keeps F's per-class multiset of slowdowns, but because sizes differ within a class, permuting slowdowns changes GPU-work: like CS (PRED-020: within about 0.5%), CO/CQ/CT match F's GPU-work only approximately. Each run records work_ratio_vs_F and the grader reports its range per arm and row.
instrument.check_before_seal: With the C-058 mode on, every pre-existing arm must reproduce the sealed E22 numbers exactly (bit-identical mean_jct) and RP must equal F (relative <= 1e-9). Done before sealing; see seal_integrity.

already_known: Fragmentation is worse when the cluster is fuller (geometric: fewer whole free nodes); known in GPU scheduling practice (Tiresias, Gandiva, Philly analyses) and bin-packing.
State-dependent service slowdowns create feedback near saturation (general queueing knowledge).
FCFS head-of-line blocking in MSJ (Grosof, Harchol-Balter, Scheller-Wolf).
prior_art.what_is_not_claimed_new: That fuller clusters fragment more (S2 is expected from geometry).
prior_art.candidate_contribution: Within this model: which link CS breaks carries fcfs's state coupling -- slowdowns placed at high occupancy (CO), at long queues (CQ), or coarse arrival-order drift (CT). Novelty UNKNOWN.

experiment.grid: trace_like, first_fit, rows (rho, pi) in {(0.55, 0.2), (0.6, 0.2), (0.6, 0.1)} x seeds 2301-2306 x horizons {160k, 320k}; fcfs arms BASE F RP CS CM U CO CQ CT; srpt BASE F U. 72 tasks, 864 simulations, CPU only.

predictions.P0: Instrument: fcfs RP mean JCT equals F within relative 1e-9 in every run. Failure stops the episode.
predictions.D: DECISION. Occupancy carries the coupling: in every decision row ((0.55, 0.2), (0.6, 0.2)) where fcfs F, CS, CO are STABLE and mean a > 0, mean d_CO >= 0.5 * mean a, d_CO = log(J_CO / J_CS). At least one such row.
predictions.S1: Occupancy beats coarse arrival order: in the same rows (CT also STABLE), mean d_CO > mean d_CT.
predictions.S2: Fuller clusters fragment more, without any slowdown (expected from geometry): in fcfs BASE at (0.6, 0.2), Spearman(excess, busy) > 0 for needs 2, 4, 8, 16 on all six seeds.
predictions.S3: The same holds in F for fcfs and for srpt.
predictions.S4: Feedback: at (0.6, 0.2), fcfs F's excess nodes per placement exceeds BASE's on all six seeds (F's slowdowns keep the cluster fuller, so later jobs land on a more fragmented cluster).
predictions.reported: CQ's share; Spearman(excess, queue length) and (excess, scatter); E21's P2 rule re-applied on these seeds (descriptive, not a third replication test).

pre_committed_consequence.D_pass_S1_pass: Within this model, the state coupling is mostly 'slowdowns land when the cluster is full': keeping each slowdown in its occupancy stratum restores at least half of a, more than coarse arrival-order blocks do. Write it as the mechanism candidate 'fragmentation concentrates at high occupancy and fcfs pays for it then'. Local arrival-order correlation inside busy periods is not separated (see unknowns).
pre_committed_consequence.D_pass_S1_fail: Occupancy strata restore half of a, but coarse arrival-order blocks restore as much or more: the coupling is time-local and occupancy is one proxy for it. Do not name occupancy as the mechanism.
pre_committed_consequence.D_fail: Occupancy at placement does not carry most of the coupling. Report the three shares as measured; do not name a mechanism.
pre_committed_consequence.D_unscorable: Do not interpret the shares; report labels.

declared_unknowns: CS, CO, CQ, CT each change GPU-work slightly (about 0.1-0.5% at 160k in the check runs; up to 1.7% for CS at 2,000 jobs in Codex's check). d_X = log(J_X/J_CS) therefore mixes a small work difference into what X restores. If any |work_ratio - 1| at 320k exceeds 0.01, this is flagged before interpreting D.
Five strata are coarse: a stratum shuffle that restores little may only mean the strata are too wide, not that the variable is irrelevant.
Occupancy and arrival order are correlated (busy periods are contiguous in time); CT with five blocks is a coarse-drift control only and does not test local order inside a busy period.
Strata are F's state; the replayed arm's own state differs once slowdowns move.
srpt has no stratified arms (it re-places jobs; per-job state is not unique).
Other mixes, loads, placements, penalty shapes; real clusters.
